THE SHARED accepted_uncovered.txt HAS NO PER-PROJECT INTEGRITY GUARD AND IS MERGED BY HAND. gen_mt_exemptions.py deliberately does NOT write the shared file; it writes its own copy and selfcheck asserts the shared file carries those lines. Verified: all 17 mt lines match the generated copy exactly, 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 malformed lines file-wide. BUT: nothing on this estate can detect the loss or corruption of ANOTHER project's lines, and there is no baseline to diff against (no VCS). I therefore CANNOT certify 'no other project's lines were touched' -- I can only report that this build's generator cannot write them and that the file is structurally intact. A per-project section digest belongs in vault_tools.

Measured, not inferred -- each line was resolved against that project's emitted satellites. Only 1 of its 35 still suppresses a real gap. maximus_travel_dv_dbt's 3 lines are all still live. This is BUILD_RULES 1.19 (a probe has a lifetime) applied to exemptions: a dead exemption is indistinguishable from a live one and silently pre-authorises future silence. NOT caused by this build; raised because this build is the one that read the file.

THE CHAIN DOES NOT REGENERATE reproducibility.json, BUT IT IS LISTED AS A CHAIN OUTPUT. prove_mt_reproducibility.CHAIN_OUTPUT_FILES includes build_artifacts/reproducibility.json, yet run_all.sh never writes it -- only the standalone prover does. Following BUILD_RULES 9.3 with that list as the definition of 'what the chain rewrites' DELETES the artifact permanently. I did exactly that and had to restore it by running the prover. This is the 9.3 incident class in a milder form. FIX: either drop it from CHAIN_OUTPUT_FILES or state that the prover must be re-run.

BUILD_STATUS.json LOSES TWO SCHEMA-REQUIRED FIELDS ON EVERY CHAIN RE-RUN. 'project' and 'generated' are in selfcheck_mt.STAGE1_OWNED_KEYS, so they are excluded from preservation -- but stage 1 never writes them (it writes lob, stage, generated_by). Net effect: the chain deletes them. Observed: I wrote the clause block, ran the chain, and both were gone while clauses/counts/gates/done survived. A BUILD_STATUS.json carrying no project name and no generation date is exactly the 'stale verdict reads as current' hazard. FIX: remove them from STAGE1_OWNED_KEYS, or have stage 1 write them. Re-added by hand; they will vanish again on the next run_all.sh.

FIX: score against canonical renderings, as the shared gate already does (109 vs 7).
